title: Delayed Repression and Emergent Instability in Adaptive Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Regulatory institutions (from content moderation platforms to financial supervisors) observe, deliberate, and intervene only after a characteristic delay. We ask whether this processing lag alone can destabilize a multi-agent system that would otherwise remain stable, without exogenous shocks, coordination among agents, or malicious actors. We study this in two stages. First, we analyze a delayed replicator equation in which autonomous agents benefit from radical behavior but face punishment based on a lagged institutional alarm signal.
